intro: Section 23.10 covers interpersonal therapy (IPT): its origins with Klerman and Weissman, the link it draws between mood and current relationships, the initial, intermediate and termination phases (Table 23-13), the four problem areas of grief, interpersonal deficits, role disputes and role transitions (Table 23-14), and group IPT and its stages (Table 23-15). A dashed box adds a 2024 patient-level comparison of IPT and antidepressants.
objectives: Describe the origins and theory of IPT.
Outline the three phases of individual IPT and their tasks (Table 23-13).
Identify the four IPT problem areas and the goals and strategies for each (Table 23-14).
Describe the structure of group IPT and its stages of group development (Table 23-15).
